outcome: Adverse perinatal outcomes (pre-eclampsia, fetal macrosomia, gestational diabetes, caesarean delivery, low birth weight, postpartum haemorrhage, admissions to special care nursery, prematurity, fetal abnormality)
cohort: 42,582 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies giving birth at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital in Sydney, Australia between January 1990 and December 2014
finding: The study found that the prevalence of overweight and obesity among nulliparous pregnant women increased over the 25-year period, leading to a rise in attributable adverse perinatal outcomes.
